title: Stop a runaway cart and set its brake before letting go
instruction: Stop the rolling cart before it runs off the end of its track, then set its brake by pushing the orange lever over toward the cart, and let go of the cart.
context: A cart left unbraked on a sloped floor, ramp or dock plate starts to roll. Stopping it is not enough: on a slope it rolls away again as soon as it is let go, so it is only safe once its parking brake (here a floor-lock lever whose rubber pad presses on the floor) is set. The robot must catch a moving load, secure it, and only then release it. Done by: warehouse, hospital and workshop staff, stagehands, anyone working with wheeled carts.
setup: The two arm bases stand 61 cm apart on an oak table. A grey painted plywood track deck (22 x 108 x 5 cm, friction about 0.6) lies across the table in front of the arms, its centre line 30 cm in front of the bases, running from 44 cm toward the right arm to 64 cm toward the left arm from the midpoint between the bases. It slopes down 1.2 degrees toward the left: its top is 3.5 cm above the table at its right end and 1.2 cm at its left end, which stops 1 cm short of the table's left edge (an open drop to the floor). On it run two steel rails (1.5 cm wide, 1 cm high, centres 4 cm either side of the centre line, low-friction PTFE tape on top) and, between them, a steel guide bar (2 cm wide, 1.6 cm high), all along its whole length. A blue plastic model cart (body 12 cm across x 16 cm long x 5 cm high, 330 g in all) stands square on the rails: two 1.5 x 14 x 1 cm runners under it slide on the rails, and two 0.8 x 10 cm guide shoes under its middle straddle the guide bar with 4 mm play each side. Its centre is 30 cm in front of the bases and 30 cm toward the right arm from their midpoint. On the cart's near side (facing the arms), 3 cm behind its middle (toward the right), an orange brake lever (12.5 cm long, 8 mm thick, 30 g) turns on a hinge 3.5 cm out from the cart's side and 4.7 cm above the deck, its axis along the track: a 3 x 4 cm paddle at the top and a black rubber pad (0.8 x 2.4 cm) at its foot, 5 cm below the hinge. At the start the brake is off: the lever leans out toward the arms at 40 degrees from upright, against its stop, its pad 6 mm above the deck. Pushed over toward the cart, past upright to its other stop 12 degrees beyond, the pad presses on the deck and lifts the cart's near side about 1 mm; the lever stays there by itself. The cart is released at rest when the trial starts. Untouched, it rolls down the track, reaches the front of the left arm about 2.1 s later at about 0.3 m/s, and runs off the end of the track and the table after 3.6 s. Stopped and let go without the brake, it rolls away again.
scoring: 1.0 if the cart stands square on its rails (within 8 mm of the centre line, within 4 degrees of the track's slope), its brake lever at least 8 degrees past upright toward the cart, still (under 5 mm/s), with every part of both arms at least 2 cm from the cart and the lever, for 2 s, and it never left the track. Otherwise, where the cart is when the trial ends: 0.75 if it is still on its rails with the brake set but an arm is within 2 cm of it; 0.5 if it is still on its rails with the brake not set (something is holding it); 0.25 if it is on the track, upright, but still moving or pushed off its rails; 0 if at any time it ran off the end of the track, was pushed or lifted off it, or if it ends tipped over or lifted more than 3 cm off the rails.
reset_notes: Set the brake lever back against its outer stop, put the cart back at its start on the rails and let it go at rest as the trial starts. On a real table, put a padded catch box on the floor under the track's end.
fidelity: The cart slides on low-friction runners, not wheels: the rails' friction (0.006) stands in for ball-bearing rolling resistance, so it accelerates down the 1.2-degree slope at about 0.15 m/s2. Cart and lever are a two-link articulation with a frictionless hinge; the brake is a springless over-centre toggle (stops, lever weight, deck on the pad) holding by pad friction (about 0.7). The cart is released at rest.
